description: A dashboard labelled Live shows numbers typed into the source file. Page views and signups are only printed, the tracking id belongs to nobody, and the figures do not change between reads.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded demo or sample datasets in production code
required_outcomes.why: demo_data is assigned a literal and is the only source the dashboard reads.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded demo analytics values in production code
required_outcomes.why: a literal tracking id is configured and no analytics service is loaded, so nothing on the page is measured.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded demo or chart values in production code
required_outcomes.why: the chart series is a literal array that is identical on every read.

required_outcomes.title: project contains placeholder user or content IDs in production code
required_outcomes.why: signups are attributed to a placeholder user id in a production path.

required_outcomes.title: project contains TODO or FIXME comments in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads a `TODO` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in, and not what the marker is on — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later`, one rank below the `should_fix_first` this outcome requires.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the TODO is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/fake-auth/scenario.json` requires `must_fix` for `CandidateCategory::Todo` at `src/auth.js` while this fixture requires `should_fix_first` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. The `should_fix_first` this fixture requires is reached by `demo_data_heuristics`, which read the constants the dashboard presents as measurements.

required_outcomes.why: the unfinished analytics wiring is marked with a TODO.

required_outcomes.title: project contains placeholder usage in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads a `placeholder` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in, and not what it stands in for — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later`, one rank below the `should_fix_first` this outcome requires.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the marker is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/dead-button/scenario.json` and `fixtures/adversarial/fake-auth/scenario.json` require `must_fix` for `CandidateCategory::Placeholder` while this fixture requires `should_fix_first` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. The `should_fix_first` this fixture requires is reached by `demo_data_heuristics`, whose `DemoDataCategory::PlaceholderUserId` row read the placeholder user id in the production path.

required_outcomes.why: the signup record is described in the source as a placeholder.
the dashboard's Live label is a claim to a user, so the constants behind it must be surfaced rather than filed away.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The dashboard is reported as showing live or real data, or the project is reported as having working analytics.
The project aggregates to green while the numbers a user reads as live are constants and analytics events go nowhere.

Ordinary constants are flagged as defects. A retry count or a page size is not demo data; what is wrong here is a constant presented as a measurement. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs holds this to exactly four demo-data proposals, so a module that flagged every literal would fail rather than pass.
The Live label, the constant figures and the discarded analytics events are not reported at all.

notes: Severity, recorded rather than measured here: evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json requires should_fix_first for this case, and should_fix_first is what demo_data_heuristics reaches for all four constants — Severity::ShouldFixFirst, critical = false, EvidenceClass::Inference. P6-T004's acceptance names exactly this fixture, so a grader should read the four demo-data detectors firing as the intended evidence. The two candidate_scanner outcomes land at can_fix_later, because that scanner reads a `TODO` or a `placeholder` as an unfinished marker and not as a constant presented as a measurement; each says so in its own `required_severity_unmet` block, which carries the reason the requirement stands unmet and what would have to change for it to be met. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts exactly these six proposals, and its every_recorded_detector_severity_is_what_the_detector_produces_today reads this file's own detector_severity_today values and runs the detector named beside each one. Before P7-T011 every scanner here emitted Severity::Note, so none of these weights was reachable; that the required and the delivered severity were once different is kept as SEVERITY_BEFORE_P7T011 in that file and in git, and the test that recorded the gap was inverted rather than deleted: it is what_is_detected_now_carries_the_weight_the_manifest_requires now, and it asserts the severity the manifest requires rather than the gap.
